name: Learning from limited or unlabeled visual data
gist: Training vision models without needing huge amounts of labeled examples, using tricks like self-supervision, transfer learning, and learning from a few examples.
explain: Collecting and labeling images is expensive and slow. To train a detector, you need thousands or millions of labeled examples, each annotated by hand — a person draws boxes around objects and labels them. But often you have lots of unlabeled images and only a handful of labeled ones. Or you have a task where labels do not exist and would be hard to define. How can you learn from limited or unlabeled data? This is not just a cost-cutting problem; it is about enabling computer vision for domains where labeling is hard or impossible, like medical imaging where each label requires a specialist.

The challenge is that neural networks are data-hungry. A model trained on ten labeled examples will overfit: it will memorize those examples rather than learn the general pattern. But unlabeled data contains signal — the distribution of images in the real world. Can you extract that signal without explicit labels? One idea is self-supervision: create labels automatically by solving a pretext task. For instance, split an image into patches, shuffle them, and train the model to reassemble them. The model learns useful features as a side effect. Another idea is transfer learning: pre-train a model on a large labeled dataset (like ImageNet), then fine-tune it on your small labeled set for your specific task. The pre-training gives the model a head start. A third idea is few-shot learning: given just a few examples of a new class, can the model learn to recognize it? This requires learning how to learn, a form of meta-learning.

Papers in this subtheme explore several directions. Some use contrastive learning: learn representations by making similar images (same object, different angles) close in embedding space and different objects far apart, without explicit class labels. Others use pseudo-labeling: make predictions on unlabeled data, keep the confident ones as labels, and retrain. Some use data augmentation: apply random transformations (crop, rotate, color shift) to images, assuming the label stays the same, so one image becomes many training examples. Others use semi-supervised learning: train on labeled and unlabeled data at the same time, using unlabeled data to constrain the shape of decision boundaries. A few use knowledge distillation: if you have a large pre-trained model, train a smaller model to imitate it, transferring knowledge even without labeled data. The goal is the same across all approaches: make computer vision work when labels are scarce.

papers.title: Is Task-Specific Training Necessary for Anomaly Detection?
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across benchmarks including 96.7% Pixel AUROC on MVTec-AD with just a single anomaly-free image.

papers.title: Learning to Label: A Reinforced Self-Evolving Framework for Semi-supervised Referring Expression Segmentation
papers.contribution: Demonstrates improved semi-supervised referring expression segmentation on RefCOCO variants through joint optimization of segmentation model and pseudo-labels under sparse supervision.

papers.title: Point-UQ: An Uncertainty-Quantification Paradigm for Point Cloud Few-Shot Class Incremental Learning
papers.contribution: Enables robust base-class knowledge retention and accurate novel-class recognition in 3D few-shot incremental learning without retraining on ModelNet, ShapeNet, and other point-cloud benchmarks.

papers.title: Rethinking Temporal Consistency in Video Object-Centric Learning: From Prediction to Correspondence
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive performance on MOVi-D, MOVi-E, and YouTube-VIS without learnable parameters for temporal modeling.

papers.title: Rethinking Unsupervised Cross-modal Flow Estimation: Learning from Decoupled Optimization and Consistency Constraint
papers.contribution: DCFlow integrates with various flow estimation networks and achieves state-of-the-art performance among unsupervised approaches on cross-modal flow benchmarks.

papers.title: 3DPoV: Improving 3D understanding via Patch Ordering on Videos
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on keypoint matching under viewpoint variation and improves diverse backbones including DINOv3 on depth and surface normal estimation.

papers.title: Anatomy-aware Representation Learning for Medical Ultrasound
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms self-supervised baselines across ultrasound diagnostic tasks including breast/thyroid cancer, cardiac view classification, and COVID-19 identification.

papers.title: Asymmetric Contrastive Objectives for Efficient Phenotypic Screening
papers.contribution: Outperforms prior methods on BBBC021, RxRx3-core, and uncurated HaCaT screens across multiple metrics with 10x smaller parameter count while maintaining improved performance.

papers.title: Beyond Blind Noising: Disentangled Visual Rectification for Hallucination Mitigation in MLLMs
papers.contribution: DVR achieves approximately $5\times$ theoretical error reduction over VCD and establishes SOTA performance on POPE, MME, LLaVA-Bench and CHAIR benchmarks

papers.title: Granularity-Aware Adaptive Classifier Expansion via Zero-Shot Learning
papers.contribution: Balances distinct and similar classes through theoretical and empirical interventions for improved zero-shot classification.

papers.title: HierLoc: Hyperbolic Entity Embeddings for Hierarchical Visual Geolocation
papers.contribution: HierLoc establishes state-of-the-art on OSV5M benchmark by reducing mean geodesic error by 19.5% while improving fine-grained subregion accuracy by 43%.

papers.title: Improving CLIP Adaptation by Breaking Tail Alignment for Source-Free Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on four challenging CDFSL benchmarks by exploiting the counterintuitive finding that pushing away tail tokens from textual embeddings improves target-domain performance.

papers.title: Must All Negatives Be Pushed Away Equally? Uncertainty-Aware Cross-View Geo-Localization via Normal Inverse Gamma Distribution
papers.contribution: Achieves 18% R@1 average improvement in zero-shot cross-dataset transfer compared to prior methods.

papers.title: Part-level Semantic-guided Contrastive Learning for Fine-grained Visual Classification
papers.contribution: The framework demonstrates superior performance and generalization ability on five publicly available FGVC datasets through modular design and synergy between vision and language.

papers.title: Pay Attention to CTC: Fast and Robust Pseudo-Labelling for Unified Speech Recognition
papers.contribution: Halves training time, improves robustness to OOD inputs, and achieves state-of-the-art on LRS3, LRS2, and WildVSR.

papers.title: Seeing What’s Not There: Negation Understanding Needs More Than Training
papers.contribution: The approach improves CLIP performance on NegBench from 25.5% to 67.0% for MCQ without expensive training, achieving state-of-the-art negation understanding.

papers.title: Semi-LAR: Semi-supervised Contrastive Learning with Linear Attention for Removal of Nighttime Flares
papers.contribution: The method consistently improves flare removal performance and robustness across multiple benchmarks in a model-agnostic manner.

papers.title: UFO-4D: Unposed Feedforward 4D reconstruction from Two Images
papers.contribution: The framework outperforms prior work by up to a factor of three while enabling high-fidelity 4D spatio-temporal interpolation from just two images.

papers.title: Vision Transformer Finetuning Benefits from Non-Smooth Components
papers.contribution: Over 1,000 finetuning runs show attention and feedforward plasticity consistently leads to better performance, departing from the prevailing smoothness preference.
